settings.headline: Numbing cream for Botox
settings.subhead: Numbing cream for Botox is a topical preparation some people use beforehand for comfort — though Botox uses very fine needles, so most describe a quick pinch rather than real pain, and many manage without any numbing at all. It reduces the sensation rather than removing it.
settings.image_alt: Senseless Professional Strength Comfort Cream and Comfort Gel — botox preparation

settings.headline: What to know
settings.body: Because Botox involves fine needles and brief injections, numbing is genuinely optional — plenty of people have it without. If you'd prefer to prepare for comfort, a cream applied to clean skin beforehand can help, with your practitioner's agreement. Numbing is preparation, not part of the treatment, and many practitioners apply their own or prefer to advise on what you use — so check with yours first. There's no need to reach for the strongest option; comfort is personal.

• Botox uses very fine needles, so most people feel a quick pinch rather than real pain — numbing is optional.
  • A topical numbing preparation beforehand can add comfort; it reduces sensation, it doesn't remove it.
  • Many practitioners apply their own numbing or prefer to advise — check before preparing your own.
  • Senseless is a UK cosmetic numbing range, formulated in the United Kingdom — not a medicine.

settings.question: Do you need numbing cream for Botox?
settings.answer: No — Botox uses fine needles and many people manage without. Some prefer a numbing preparation for added comfort; it's optional.

settings.question: Can you use numbing cream before Botox?
settings.answer: Often yes, for comfort — but check with your practitioner first, as many numb the skin themselves or prefer to advise.

settings.question: Does Botox hurt without numbing?
settings.answer: Most people describe a quick pinch or sting rather than real pain, because the needles are very fine.

settings.question: Is numbing cream safe before Botox?
settings.answer: Used as directed on clean, healthy skin it's widely used; patch test first and check with your practitioner.
